resources.string: This is a development installation with the DevTools plugin.
The Admidio command line in the browser, with the documentation of every command, grouped by area.

Tools for developers, reviewers and translators: snapshots of files and database, hook inspector and trace, logs and exceptions, CLI task runner, mail catcher, preferences diff, organization and language switch, plugin scaffolder. Only active with $gDebug = true in config.php.
Store every exception that ends a request, with stack trace, URL and the names of the request parameters, so that it can be analysed later.
Keeping exceptions is switched off in the settings of the plugin.
All registered hook callbacks with owner and source, the places in core and plugins that dispatch hooks, and the problems both show together.
Nothing in the code dispatches this hook.
No trace has been recorded yet.
The hook registry of this Admidio version cannot be read.
The hook callbacks the last requests ran, in order, with duration and arguments, and for filters the value before and after.
Record the hook callbacks of every request. Costs some time per request; the last 50 requests are kept.
Recording of hook traces is switched off.
The hook #VAR1# has a callback (#VAR2#), but nothing dispatches it. A typo, or the hook exists only on another branch?
The plugin #VAR2# dispatches the hook #VAR1# without its plugin ID as prefix (#VAR3#).
Several owners change the filter #VAR1#: #VAR2#. They run in the order of the registrations.
The log files of Admidio, of the command line and of core updates, the PHP error log, and the exceptions that ended requests.
The mails Admidio sent while the mail catcher was active, with HTML preview, text and the complete message.
Catch: no mail leaves the system
On a copy of real member data one test mail can reach hundreds of real people. "Catch" keeps every mail here, "Redirect" delivers every mail to one address only.
Redirect: every mail goes to one address
The address that receives every mail in the mode "Redirect". Without a valid address mails are caught.
The maintenance jobs of core and plugins, when they ran, whether cron still runs them, and running them now.
From the log of the command line. Exit code 6 means that at least one job failed; run the jobs here to see which one. The core keeps no results per job.
The log of the command line shows no run of maintenance:run in the last #VAR1# days. Is cron set up?
Overdue: the regular runs have stopped.
The DevTools only work on a development installation. Set $gDebug = true in adm_my_files/config.php.
Tools for developing and testing Admidio and its plugins. This installation is marked as a development installation ($gDebug).
Path of the PHP binary that runs the Admidio command line from the browser. Empty: found automatically.
The preferences of an organization compared with their defaults: changed values, missing rows, and rows nobody defines any more.
Click a status to show or hide its preferences.
not loaded here; default from its plugin.json
I know that the files and the database of this installation will be replaced.
A snapshot is restored on a page of its own that works without Admidio, even when an update broke the installation. Bookmark it and keep the key.
The snapshot was restored. The logins were kept.
The snapshot was restored. All sessions have ended; log in again.
Restores the files and the database of this Admidio installation from a snapshot of the DevTools plugin. This page works without Admidio.
The form is invalid. Load the page again.
Keep the current logins (sessions and "remember me") instead of those of the snapshot
The DevTools snapshot page shows the key. It is also stored in the file #VAR1# in the snapshot directory.
The key is created with the first snapshot.
A new restore key was created. The old one is no longer valid.
Restoring is only possible on a development installation ($gDebug = true in adm_my_files/config.php).
The plugin was created in #VAR1#. Install it in the plugin manager.

Creates the skeleton of a new plugin that follows the conventions of the example plugin hello-world: manifest, entry file, language files in English and German, and optionally a page, a setting, a CLI command, a test and the GitHub release workflow.
Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. It is also the name of the directory.
The setting applies to the current organization.
A snapshot keeps the files and the database of this installation. Take one before you update to a pull request, test, and restore it before the next one.

An absolute path, ideally outside the web root, or a path inside adm_my_files. Empty: adm_my_files/snapshots. It is kept in adm_my_files/devtools/snapshot-path.php, which no restore touches; $gDevToolsSnapshotPath in config.php takes precedence.
The directory is set with $gDevToolsSnapshotPath in adm_my_files/config.php and can only be changed there.
The directory is inside the Admidio directory. It is protected by .htaccess, which only Apache honours.
The web server cannot write into #VAR1#.
Uploads, photos, documents and other data. Without it only config.php and cli-config.php of adm_my_files are part of the snapshot.
Click a column to sort by it, Shift+click to add it as a further sort key, click again to reverse.
Commands act as #VAR1# in the organization #VAR2#, unless the command line says otherwise.
Runs as a separate process with the rights and the log of the command line. Destructive commands need --yes.
